messages:
nora: Quick note — onboarding aurora-lite-6B (converted from Gemma-format) shows word shuffle after int4. Short repro below.

ben: Minimal prompt + outputs? and converter flags?

nora: Prompt: "Why is the sky blue?"
nora: Gemma float32: "Rayleigh scattering scatters shorter wavelengths, making sky look blue during day."
nora: Converted+int4: "Sky scattering shorter blue during day looks Rayleigh making."  <-- words reordered.

hiro: That looks like position-dependent phase misalignment. Any tokenizer diffs (emoji/diacritic handling)?

nora: Short prompts tokenized same, but longer examples with emojis split differently: source -> [500,12,900] target -> [500,4,8,12,900]. Extra subtokens shift rotary phases.

ci-bot: Mini metrics: ppl 11.8 -> 15.9, summary-sim 0.48 -> 0.30.

sam: Two likely causes: tokenizer normalization (NFKC) and head-order swap in converter reshape. Check the reshape/order used when splitting heads.

ben: Found converter bug: reshape used implicit order leading to head0/head1 swap for certain layer shapes. Fixing reshape+transpose and forcing tokenizer normalize nfkc improves results.

nora: After patch + re-quant: ppl 12.0, sim 0.46. PR opened with unit test for tokenization round-trip + head-index dump.

hiro: Add --preserve-rotary-order flag and make tokenizer-normalize nfkc default for Gemma imports until auto-detect exists.

nora: Agree. I'll add small eval prompts to onboarding dir and a CI check comparing float32 vs int4 semantics.

ci-bot: CI: unit tests added tests/rotary_token_roundtrip.py, local pass.
